title: Bronchiolitis and Infant Respiratory Distress: Assessment and Admission Criteria

evidenceAudit.scope: Clinical diagnosis, severity assessment, supportive care and disposition for babies and children with bronchiolitis.
findings: The named primary guideline was opened and the cited sections were used.
Normal values are descriptive; use local laboratory and age/pregnancy ranges.
unverifiedSections: No topic-specific Saudi national guideline was identified in the opened Saudi MOH protocol index.
SFDA registration and hospital formulary availability were not verified; no drug dose is supplied.

pathophysiology.summary: Viral inflammation and mucus obstruct small airways. Air trapping and atelectasis impair gas exchange. Young infants can fatigue, feed poorly and develop apnoea.
keyMechanisms: Viral inflammation and mucus obstruct small airways.
Air trapping and atelectasis impair gas exchange.
Young infants can fatigue, feed poorly and develop apnoea.

symptoms: Coryzal prodrome followed by cough, tachypnoea, feeding difficulty and wheeze or crackles.
physicalSigns: Increased respiratory effort, recession, nasal flaring, crackles or wheeze and reduced intake.
redFlags: Apnoea, cyanosis, severe distress, exhaustion, reduced consciousness, dehydration or persistent low oxygen saturation.
precipitants: Respiratory viral infection; severity risk is higher in very young or premature infants and those with chronic lung, cardiac, neuromuscular or immune disease.

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Recurrent episodic wheeze without crackles, especially in an older infant/child.
High fever or persistently focal crackles.
Sudden onset or focal unilateral findings.
Hepatomegaly, murmur, poor growth or pulmonary oedema pattern.

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Coryzal prodrome for 1–3 days followed by persistent cough plus tachypnoea or recession and wheeze or crackles (NG9 1.1).

ruleIn.normalValue: At or above the age/risk-specific target
ruleIn.expectedFinding: Persistent saturation below the admission or oxygen threshold
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Measure in every suspected case; interpret with clinical severity and risk factors.

clinicalManagement.title: Assess breathing and feeding
actions: Record oxygen saturation, work of breathing, apnoea history, hydration and risk factors.
Escalate apnoea, exhaustion, cyanosis or severe distress to paediatric critical care.

clinicalManagement.title: Provide supportive care
actions: Use minimal handling and nasal suction only when secretions impair breathing or feeding.
Provide enteral or intravenous isotonic fluid when oral intake is inadequate according to the paediatric fluid pathway.

clinicalManagement.title: Choose admission or discharge
actions: Admit when oxygenation, apnoea, hydration, work of breathing, risk factors or caregiver/social circumstances make home care unsafe.
Do not use antibiotics, bronchodilators, adrenaline or corticosteroids routinely for bronchiolitis.

medicationPlan.note: Routine medicines are not indicated in uncomplicated bronchiolitis; oxygen and fluids are supportive treatments governed by the paediatric protocol.

teaching.scope: Clinical diagnosis, severity assessment, supportive care and disposition for babies and children with bronchiolitis.
learningObjectives: Recognise the condition and its red flags.
Choose initial tests without delaying urgent escalation.
Use a named multidisciplinary disposition plan.

pitfalls: Delaying escalation while waiting for non-essential tests.
Using an unverified medicine regimen instead of the current local protocol.

patientEducation: Explain the working diagnosis, immediate plan and specific return or deterioration signs.
lifestyleAndDiet: Address prevention and self-management only after the acute safety plan is complete.
dischargeCriteria: Clinically stable, maintaining age/risk-appropriate oxygen saturation in air, taking adequate fluids and caregivers understand red flags.
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Give return advice for apnoea, cyanosis, worsening effort, exhaustion or poor intake; arrange review for high-risk infants as locally required.
